activities.title: Start here
activities.instruction: Understand an API as an agreed way for one piece of software to ask another piece of software for information or an operation.

content.title: APIs Are Agreements
content.hook: So far, your browser has mostly been dealing with pages.
content.context:
Now imagine a page that needs weather information, a list of products, or the current account profile.

Where does that information come from?

One useful answer is: **another piece of software provides it.**

An **API** is a defined way for software to communicate.

Think of it like a counter at a busy shop.

You do not walk into the kitchen and start rearranging the shelves.

You make a request in the form the shop accepts.

The kitchen does its work.

You get a response.

The important idea is not the restaurant metaphor itself.

The important idea is this:

**An API gives software a way to ask for something and know what kind of answer to expect.**
goals: Understand an API as an agreed way for one piece of software to ask another piece of software for information or an operation.

content.question:
A weather application needs today's temperature.

Which statement best describes the role of an API here?

options.text: The API is a way for the application to communicate with another system using an agreed format.
The API is the screen color of the weather application.
The API is the browser's memory.
The API is the keyboard shortcut used to refresh the page.

feedback.correct: An API is a communication contract. It defines how software can ask for something and what kind of information or operation is available.
feedback.incorrect: An API is a communication contract. It defines how software can ask for something and what kind of information or operation is available.

content.title: The contract idea
content.text:
A useful API usually answers questions like:

- What can I ask for?
- How do I ask for it?
- What information do I need to send?
- What will come back?
- What does an error mean?

Suppose an API offers a route called:

```text
/products
```

The name alone is not the whole contract.

A useful contract might tell you that a request to `/products` returns a list of products.

That means frontend code does not have to guess what the other system decided to send.

content.question:
Imagine an API contract says:

```text
GET /products
returns:
[
  { "name": "Notebook" },
  { "name": "Keyboard" }
]
```

The frontend expects a list.

What would be most useful for the frontend developer?

options.text: Knowing the shape of the data that comes back.
Knowing the color of the server room.
Knowing the keyboard shortcut used by the backend developer.
Knowing the font used in the API documentation.

feedback.correct: Shared expectations about the data shape are part of the contract.
feedback.incorrect: Shared expectations about the data shape are part of the contract.

content.question:
A developer writes code that expects each product to have a `name`.

The API changes and now returns:

```text
[
  { "title": "Notebook" },
  { "title": "Keyboard" }
]
```

What changed?

options.text: The contract the frontend relied on no longer matches the data it receives.

feedback.correct: The issue is not “the data is wrong” in some abstract sense. The issue is that the consumer expected one shape and received another.
feedback.incorrect: The issue is not “the data is wrong” in some abstract sense. The issue is that the consumer expected one shape and received another.

activities.title: Say it in your own words
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt:
Complete:

> “An API is useful because it gives two pieces of software a shared ________ for communicating.”
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.

feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

content.question: Which sentence best captures the idea of an API?

options.text: “An API is where the data lives.”
“An API is an agreed way for software to communicate.”
“An API is another word for a webpage.”

feedback.correct: Keep the distinction clear: an API is a communication interface, not a programming language and not necessarily a webpage.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the distinction clear: an API is a communication interface, not a programming language and not necessarily a webpage.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** APIs are agreements between software.
**Senior habit:** When integrating with another system, ask first: “What is the contract?”
nextSteps: Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain why a consumer and provider need matching expectations.
